• • 3-4 lbs. center cut pork roast – (ask the butcher to saw across the rib bones of the roast, at the base of the backbone – separating the ribs from the backbone. It will ease the carving).
  • • 2 cups chicken stock
  • • 2 teaspoons caraway seeds
  • • 3 cloves garlic, pressed
  • • 2 bay leaves
  • • salt and pepper
Pork roast - Vepřová pečeně
In a saucepan heat the chicken stock, caraway seeds, bay leaves and garlic.

Rinse and pat dry the meat and rub it with salt and pepper. Place it, skin down, on a rack in an open roasting pan. Pour half of the liquid from the saucepan over the meat and roast at 350F for 1 hour, basting frequently with the juices from the pan and the liquid from the saucepan. Turn the meat and continue roasting for 1-1/2 hours, until the top is golden brown and the meat tender. Allow 35 minutes per pound.
When done let it rest 5 minutes, carve.
Skim fat from the pan drippings, strain some over the roast, serve the rest in a saucedish.
Serve with dumplings, potato dumplings, boiled potatoes and sauerkraut.
Serves 6 – Preparation time: 3 hours
Fresh ham in cream sauce - Vepřová kýta na smetaně

• • 3-4 lbs. fresh ham, boned and skinned
  • • 4 slices bacon
  • • 6 tablespoons butter
  • • 2 carrots
  • • 1 celery root
  • • 1 parsnip
  • • 3 bay leaves, thyme, whole allspice, whole black pepper
  • • 1 lemon
  • • 1-1/2 cups sour cream
  • • 2 tablespoons flour
  • • 1-1/2 cups chicken stock or water
  • • salt
Dice the carrots, celery root and parsnip. Cut the bacon into short strips.
Skim off fat from the meat, rinse and pat it dry, salt it and lard with bacon strips.
In a large stewpot combine melted butter, vegetables, spices, lemon rind, grated or chopped.
Set over medium heat. Add the meat and brown it lightly on all sides. Lower the heat, cover tightly and simmer over low heat until tender, about 2 hours, gradually adding the chicken stock or water.
Remove meat from pot, keep it warm.
Strain the gravy into a saucepan. Combine flour and sour cream and

<content-ref src='/page/13/PageHeader/0'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/13/Text/1'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/13/Text/2'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/13/SectionHeader/3'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/13/ListGroup/4'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/13/Text/5'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/13/Text/6'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/13/Text/7'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/13/Text/8'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/13/Text/9'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/13/Text/10'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/13/PageFooter/11'></content-ref>

blend it into the gravy. Add lemon juice, simmer 5 minutes.
Slice meat, pour the gravy over it or serve separately.
Serve with dumplings, noodles, vegetables.
Serves 6 – Preparation time: 3 hours
Pork chops with caraway seeds - Vepřová žebírka na kmíně

• • 6 pork chops
  • • 1/2 cup flour
  • • 1/2 cup vegetable oil
  • • 2 tablespoons butter
  • • 1 cup chicken stock
  • • 1 small onion
  • • 2 teaspoons caraway seeds
  • • salt

Pound the pork chops lightly-they should not be more than 1/2" thick. Make a few short cuts on the edges to prevent curling, salt them on both sides and dust with flour on one side. Brown chops in hot oil, floured side first.
In a large skillet combine the butter and finely chopped onion and set over medium heat.
When the onion becomes translucent, add caraway seeds and some of the chicken stock. Add the pork chops and simmer about 30 minutes or until they are tender.
Remove the chops, bring the liquid to boil, blend in flour and chicken stock and simmer until the sauce thickens. The sauce should be medium thick. Strain.

Return pork chops in the sauce, simmer until heated through.
Serve with boiled potatoes, rice, salad.
Serves 6 – Preparation time: 45 minutes

Breaded pork chops - Vepřová žebírka smažená

• • 6 pork loin rib chops, cut about 1/2" thick
  • • 1/2 cup flour
  • • 2 eggs
  • • 1 cup bread crumbs
  • • 1 cup vegetable oil
  • • salt and pepper
Pound the pork chops lightly; make a few short cuts on the edges to prevent curling.
Spice them with salt and pepper. Dredge them in flour shaking off excess, dip in beaten eggs and coat with bread crumbs.
Fry the chops in a covered pan for 5 minutes, turn them and finish frying uncovered. Drain on paper towel.
Serve with potato salad, green salad, vegetables.
Serves 6 – Preparation time: 45 minutes
Smoked pork loin - Uzené vepřové maso

• • 2-3 lbs. fully cooked smoked pork loin or shoulder
  • • water
Place meat in boiling water and simmer until thoroughly heated.
About 30 minutes. To serve, cut meat into slices.
Serve with boiled potatoes and sauerkraut, mashed potatoes, vegetables, poached apples, salad.
Serves 6 – Preparation time: 40 minutes

• • 3 lbs. boned pork shoulder, cut in 1-1/2" cubes
  • • 1/4 cup vegetable oil
  • • 1 large onion, chopped
  • • 2 tablespoons vinegar
  • • 2 tablespoons paprika
  • • 1 teaspoon caraway seeds
  • • 2 cups beef stock
  • • 4 tablespoons flour
  • • 3/4 cup sour cream
  • • salt and pepper
Pork goulash - Guláš vepřový

Sauté onion in oil. Add paprika, vinegar, pork, caraway seeds, pepper, few spoons of beef stock. Cover and simmer 1-1/2 hrs, or until meat is tender. Stir occasionally and gradually add beef stock, little at a time, just enough to keep moisture in the stew.
Blend flour, sour cream and 1/2 cup beef stock. Stir the mixture in the pan with the meat. Simmer 10-15 minutes. If the sauce is too thick, add more beef stock.
Taste for salt. Should you prefer to redden the color of the sauce, add 2-3 tablespoons tomato paste.
Serve with potatoes or dumplings.
Serves 6 – Preparation time: 2 hours
Goulash with sauerkraut - Guláš s kyselým zelím

• • 3 lbs. boned pork shoulder, cut in 1-1/2" cubes
  • • 4 tablespoons vegetable oil
  • • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • • 2 tablespoons paprika
  • • 1 teaspoon caraway seeds
  • • 2 tablespoons vinegar
  • • 1 lb. sauerkraut
  • • 1 cup heavy cream
  • • 1 large raw potato, peeled, grated or finely sliced,
  • • salt and pepper,
  • • water

Sauté onion in oil until translucent. Sprinkle paprika evenly over onion, add pork, vinegar, caraway seeds, salt and pepper, 1/4 cup water. Cover and simmer until meat is almost tender, about 1 hr. 15 minutes. Occasionally add 1-2 tablespoons water, just enough to keep moisture in the stew. Stir and turn pork after each addition.
Stir sauerkraut into the goulash, blend in cream and potato. Simmer 10-15 minutes, or until meat is tender. Add salt, pepper and more paprika if desired.
Serve with crouton dumplings, boiled potatoes.
Serves 6 – Preparation time: 2 hours

Leg of lamb in wine sauce - Skopová kýta dušená

• • 3-4 lbs. lamb leg, boned, skinned (4-5 lbs. with bone)
  • • 1/3 cup vegetable oil
  • • 5 slices bacon
  • • 1/2 teaspoon each of ginger and ground nutmeg
  • • salt and pepper
  • • 1 parsnip, 3 carrots, 1 celery root,
  • • 1 medium onion
  • • 3 bay leaves, whole allspice, whole black pepper
  • • 3 tablespoons flour
  • • juice of 1 lemon
  • • 1/4 cup cranberry juice, unsweetened
  • • 1 cup dry red wine
  • • 1-2 cups chicken stock
Slice thinly parsnip, carrots, celery root and onion.
Cut the bacon into short strips.
Trim off excess fat from the meat, lard it with bacon (= make small slits in roast and push a strip of bacon into each slit).
Mix salt, pepper, ginger, nutmeg. Rub over lamb.
Heat the oil in a large stewpot, add the sliced vegetables, cook five minutes.
Place the lamb in the pot, brown it lightly, sprinkle with the remaining spices.
Cover and simmer 1 hour, gradually adding chicken stock.
Remove the lamb.
Spoon fat from the juices, stir in flour and cook until lightly browned.
Blend in lemon juice, cranberry juice, wine, chicken stock.
Return lamb to the mixture, cover and simmer until tender for about 1 hour.
Place lamb on a warm serving platter, garnish with mint, cranberries, snipped parsley, chestnuts.
Strain the sauce, heat thoroughly, serve in a saucedish.
Serve with rice, noodles, vegetables, potatoes.

<content-ref src='/page/17/PageHeader/0'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/17/SectionHeader/1'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/17/Text/2'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/17/Text/3'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/17/SectionHeader/4'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/17/ListGroup/5'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/17/Text/6'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/17/Text/7'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/17/Text/8'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/17/SectionHeader/9'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/17/ListGroup/10'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/17/Text/11'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/17/Text/12'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/17/Text/13'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/17/Text/14'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/17/Text/15'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/17/PageFooter/16'></content-ref>
Leg of lamb in cream sauce - Skopová kýta na smetaně
Follow instructions for Leg of lamb in wine sauce.
At the time of adding lemon juice, cranberry juice and red wine, substitute 1 cup sour cream for chicken stock.
Mutton goulash - Guláš skopový

• • 3 lbs. boned shoulder of mutton, cut in pieces, about 1-1/2"
  • • 2 tablespoons vegetable oil
  • • 5 oz. bacon, diced
  • • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • • 5 cloves garlic, pressed or chopped
  • • 2 tablespoons paprika
  • • 1 teaspoon each of caraway seeds and marjoram
  • • 3 tablespoons flour
  • • salt and pepper
Follow instructions for "Beef goulash"
Serve with potatoes, gnocchi, etc.
Serves 6 - Preparation time: 2 hours
Roast chicken - Kuře pečené

• • 1 roasting chicken, 4.5 lbs.
  • • 4 tablespoons butter
  • • 2 slices bacon
  • • 1-1/2 cups chicken stock
  • • salt and pepper

Rinse and pat dry the chicken; season with salt and pepper. Place it on rack in a shallow roasting pan, breast down. Melt the butter and sprinkle some over the chicken. Pour half of the chicken stock into a roasting pan. Cook 30 minutes in 350F oven.

Turn chicken breast up, lay bacon slices on top and continue baking 30-40 minutes until golden brown on top. Baste occasionally with the remaining butter and chicken stock, juices from the pan, or water.
Let stand 5 minutes before cutting into serving portions.
Serve with mashed potatoes, vegetables, salad, compote, mushrooms.

<content-ref src='/page/18/PageHeader/0'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/18/SectionHeader/1'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/18/ListGroup/2'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/18/Text/3'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/18/Text/4'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/18/Text/5'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/18/Text/6'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/18/SectionHeader/7'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/18/ListGroup/8'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/18/Text/9'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/18/Text/10'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/18/Text/11'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/18/Text/12'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/18/Text/13'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/18/Text/14'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/18/Text/15'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/18/Text/16'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/18/PageFooter/17'></content-ref>
Breaded chicken - Smažené kuře

• • 1 broiler-fryer chicken, 4-5 lbs., cut in serving pieces or
  • • 12 chicken thighs
  • • 3/4 cup flour
  • • 2 eggs
  • • 1-1/2 cups bread crumbs
  • • 1-1/2 cups oil for frying
  • • salt

Rinse and pat dry chicken pieces, salt them lightly. Dredge each piece in flour, shake off excess, dip in beaten eggs with a little salt added and coat with bread crumbs. Fry in hot oil until golden, about 5 minutes each side. Drain on paper towel.
Serve on lettuce-lined platter, garnish with lemon wedges and parsley.
Serve with potato salad, green salad, mashed potatoes, vegetables.
Serves 6 – Preparation time: 45 minutes
Chicken paprika - Kuře na paprice

• • 1 chicken, 4-5 lbs., cut up into small serving portions or
  • • 12 chicken thighs
  • • 6 tablespoons butter
  • • 1 medium onion, finely chopped
  • • 2 tablespoons vinegar
  • • 3 tablespoons paprika
  • • 1 cup chicken broth
  • • 1-1/2 cups sour cream
  • • 2 tablespoons flour
  • • salt and pepper

In a large heavy skillet sauté onion in butter until translucent. Stir in paprika and vinegar. Lay chicken pieces on top, cover, and simmer until almost tender, about 20 minutes. Gradually add chicken broth, if needed. Cooking liquid should be just enough that onion and chicken do not burn.
Using a slotted spoon remove chicken pieces.
Blend flour and sour cream, stir into liquid in pan, and add remaining chicken broth. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Return chicken to pan, simmer until tender but not overcooked, 5-10 minutes.
Season to taste with salt and pepper. Sauce should be medium thick and mildly piquant.
Serve with rice, noodles, gnocchi, salad.

Chicken ragoût - Ragoût z kuřete

• • 2 lbs. chicken breast, boned, skin removed
  • • soup vegetables (carrot, parsley, onion, celery)
  • • salt and pepper
  • • 1 cup sliced fresh mushrooms
  • • 2 tablespoons butter
  • • 1 small cauliflower
  • • juice of 1-2 lemons
  • • 2 egg yolks
  • • 2 tablespoons butter and 3 tablespoons flour for the roux.

• • 4 tablespoons butter
  • • chicken ragoût
  • • 1/2 cup grated Parmesan
  • • 1/2 cup bread crumbs

Cook chicken and soup vegetables in lightly salted boiling water. When cool enough to handle, dice the chicken, discard soup vegetables, reserve the broth. While the chicken cooks, heat 2 tablespoons butter in a skillet and sauté the mushrooms over medium heat (about 4 minutes) – must not be too soft. Remove from heat and reserve. Cook cauliflower in lightly salted boiling water – do not overcook, must be tender, not mushy. Drain and separate in rosettes. Reserve. In a large skillet melt the remaining 2 tablespoons butter, add 3 tablespoons flour and stir over low/medium heat until golden brown. Add 1-1/2 cups of the reserved chicken broth and simmer, uncovered, until the mixture thickens, 5-10 minutes. Add juice of 1 lemon, diced chicken, simmer 2 minutes. Blend in egg yolks, mushrooms and cauliflower rosettes. Season to taste with salt, pepper, more lemon juice. If the ragoût is too thick, add a little more chicken broth. Serve as is with boiled potatoes, lettuce.
Serves 6 – Preparation time: 1 hour
or serve au gratin:

Transfer the mixture into a buttered gratin dish, or casserole, top with grated Parmesan and bread crumbs. Sprinkle with melted butter. Bake in hot oven (400F), 10-15 minutes, or until the top is golden brown. Serve with french bread, bread sticks, lettuce.

<content-ref src='/page/20/PageHeader/0'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/20/SectionHeader/1'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/20/ListGroup/2'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/20/Text/3'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/20/Text/4'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/20/Text/5'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/20/SectionHeader/6'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/20/ListGroup/7'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/20/Text/8'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/20/Text/9'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/20/Text/10'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/20/Text/11'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/20/Text/12'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/20/Text/13'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/20/Text/14'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/20/Text/15'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/20/PageFooter/16'></content-ref>
Chicken ragoût on a half shell - as an appetizer - Ragoût na mušlich

• • Chicken ragoût
  • • 4 tablespoons butter
  • • 1/2 cup grated Parmesan
  • • 1/2 cup bread crumbs
  • • 12 shells
Butter the shells, fill each little over half full with chicken ragoût, sprinkle with grated Parmesan, bread crumbs and melted butter. Bake at 400F about 15 minutes or until golden on top.
Serves 12 as an appetizer
Preparation time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Roast turkey - Krocan pečený

• • 1 turkey, 15 lbs.
  • • 8 tablespoons (1 stick) butter
  • • 2 cups chicken broth
  • • 2 slices bacon
  • • salt
Rinse turkey with cold water, and pat dry inside and out with paper towel.
Rub the body and neck cavities with salt and butter. Brush skin with butter.
Preheat oven to 350F.
Pour one cup chicken broth in a roasting pan. Place the bird in the pan, breast down. Roast, uncovered 1-1/2 hours, basting occasionally with butter, chicken broth and pan drippings.
Turn turkey breast up, place 2 slices bacon on top and roast 1-1/2 – 2 hours, basting with the remaining butter, chicken broth and juices from the pan.

When done, transfer the bird on a heated platter. Strain the pan drippings, discarding all fat, and pour some over the turkey. Serve the remaining juice in a saucedish. For easier carving allow turkey to stand 10-15 minutes.
Serve with potatoes, salad, vegetables, compote.
Serves 15 – Preparation time: 3 hours 30 minutes

<content-ref src='/page/21/PageHeader/0'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/21/SectionHeader/1'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/21/Text/2'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/21/SectionHeader/3'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/21/ListGroup/4'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/21/Text/5'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/21/Text/6'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/21/Text/7'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/21/SectionHeader/8'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/21/ListGroup/9'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/21/Text/10'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/21/Text/11'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/21/Text/12'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/21/PageFooter/13'></content-ref>
Stuffed turkey - Krocan nadivaný

Prepare the bird as indicated in "roast turkey". Turn the neck into the body cavity to block the passage between the neck and the body. The stuffing will stay in the neck cavity while roasting. Lightly fill neck cavity with stuffing. Do not pack - stuffing will expand while cooking. Fasten neck skin with stitches or skewer. Roast turkey as shown above.
Giblets stuffing:

• • Giblets from the turkey
  • • 3 hard baked rolls
  • • 1 cup milk or water
  • • 2 whole eggs
  • • 1 small onion, chopped
  • • 4 tablespoons butter
  • • 1/2 cup bread crumbs
  • • salt, marjoram, thyme
Soak the rolls in milk or water, squeeze off excess liquid, shred them. Rinse and finely chop the giblets.
In a bowl cream butter, eggs, add the chopped onion, thyme, marjoram, shredded rolls, giblets, bread crumbs. Salt the mixture and mix thoroughly.
Preparation time: 30 minutes
Chestnuts stuffing:

• • 1 lb. chestnuts
  • • 10 tablespoons butter
  • • 4 eggs
  • • 5 hard baked rolls
  • • 2 cups milk
  • • 1/2 cup bread crumbs
  • • dash of ground nutmeg
  • • 1/2 teaspoon sugar
  • • salt
Simmer chestnuts in water for 10-15 minutes. When the shells crack, peel and chop them coarsely.

Break the rolls, soak them in milk, squeeze off excess, shred them. In a bowl cream butter, one whole egg and three egg yolks. Add the shredded rolls, nutmeg, sugar and coarsely chopped chestnuts. Salt the mixture; Fold in half of the bread crumbs and three stiffly whipped egg whites.
Turn the stuffing into a fluted tube pan or a flan ring, buttered and

<content-ref src='/page/22/PageHeader/0'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/22/Text/1'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/22/Text/2'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/22/Text/3'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/22/Text/4'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/22/SectionHeader/5'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/22/ListGroup/6'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/22/Text/7'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/22/Text/8'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/22/Text/9'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/22/Text/10'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/22/SectionHeader/11'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/22/Text/12'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/22/PageFooter/13'></content-ref>
dusted with bread crumbs. Bake in a bain-marie at 350F for 1-1/2 hours. When done, let it stand 5 minutes, then invert on a serving dish. Slice it like a cake.
Serve with apricot or pear compote, cranberries, etc.
Preparation time: 2 hours
(Have chestnuts ready ahead of time. Bake stuffing while roasting turkey, so that both will be done at the same time).
Almond stuffing:

• • 5 oz. chopped or sliced almonds
  • • 8 tablespoons butter
  • • 4 egg yolks, 3 egg whites
  • • 5 hard baked rolls
  • • 2 cups milk
  • • 1/4 cup sugar
  • • 1/4 cup bread crumbs
  • • salt
Break the rolls and soak them in milk. Squeeze off excess, shred and strain them.
In a bowl cream butter, egg yolks and sugar. Combine all ingredients. Fold in three stiffly beaten egg whites.
Bake and serve in the same manner as chestnut stuffing.
Preparation time: 2 hours
Raisins stuffing:
Same as almond stuffing, replacing half of the almonds with 3/4 cup golden raisins.

<content-ref src='/page/23/PageHeader/0'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/23/SectionHeader/1'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/23/SectionHeader/2'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/23/ListGroup/3'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/23/SectionHeader/4'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/23/ListGroup/5'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/23/Text/6'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/23/Text/7'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/23/Text/8'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/23/Text/9'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/23/Text/10'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/23/Text/11'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/23/Text/12'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/23/Text/13'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/23/SectionHeader/14'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/23/ListGroup/15'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/23/Text/16'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/23/Text/17'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/23/Text/18'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/23/PageFooter/19'></content-ref>
Stuffed pigeon - Holub nadivaný
Prepare stuffing first:

• • 3 young pigeons
  • • 6 tablespoons butter
  • • salt
  • • 3/4 cup chicken stock
Stuffing:

• • 4 and 2 tablespoons butter (2. tbsp for braising the liver)
  • • 2 egg yolks
  • • 1 egg white
  • • 2 hard baked rolls
  • • 1/2 cup milk
  • • liver from three pigeons, chopped
  • • parsley
  • • 1/2 cup bread crumbs
  • • salt

Soak the rolls in milk, squeeze off excess, shred them. Cream the butter and the egg yolks, add the shredded rolls, the liver sautéed in butter, salt, snipped parsley, bread crumbs. Add stiffly whipped egg white.
Carefully loosen the skin of the breasts and fill the pockets with stuffing. Enclose with stitches.
Salt the pigeons. Place them in a roasting pan with melted butter, breasts down, roast at 350F for 20 minutes.
Baste with melted butter, juices from the pan and a little chicken stock.
Turn pigeons breasts up and finish roasting in the same manner.
To serve, cut the pigeons in halves, sprinkle with pan drippings and snipped parsley. (Remove the stitches, of course).
Serve with potatoes, green peas, salad, etc.
Serves 6 - Preparation time: 1 hour
Roast goose - Husa pečená

• • 1 goose, 10 lbs.
  • • 4-5 medium apples
  • • salt, caraway seeds
  • • water
Rinse goose, pat dry. Rinse the apples do not peel them. Rub the goose inside and out with salt and caraway seeds. Fill body cavity with apples.
Place goose in a roasting pan with a little hot water at the bottom.
Roast at 350F, first breast side down for 1-1/2 hrs, basting with water and pan drippings. When golden brown on top, turn goose breast side

<content-ref src='/page/24/Text/0'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/24/Text/1'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/24/SectionHeader/2'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/24/ListGroup/3'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/24/Text/4'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/24/SectionHeader/5'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/24/ListGroup/6'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/24/Text/7'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/24/PageFooter/8'></content-ref>

up. Continue roasting for 1-1/2 hours. While roasting, prick the skin with a fork over the fatty areas to release fat. (Just the skin, not the meat. If the juice from the meat runs out, the goose will become dry.) Total roasting time is approximately 20 minutes per pound. During the last 15 minutes of roasting, raise oven temperature to 400F and stop basting to achieve a crunchy skin. Remove apples and slice goose. Skim fat from pan juices and pour into a gravy boat to accompany goose. Serve with dumplings, potato dumplings, cabbage, red cabbage, sauerkraut.
Serves 8-10 – Preparation time: 3 hours 30 minutes
Roast duck - Kachna pečená

• • 1 duck (approx 8 lbs.)
  • • 4 tablespoons butter
  • • salt, caraway seeds

Roast the duck in the same manner as the goose. Do not stuff with apples.
While roasting, baste often with butter.
Duckling with Madeira wine - Kachna na vině

• • 1 duckling, 5-6 lbs.
  • • 5 slices ham, cut in stripes
  • • 8 tablespoons butter
  • • 1 cup Madeira wine
  • • 1 cup chicken stock
  • • 3 tablespoons flour
  • • salt and pepper

Rinse duckling, pat dry. Sprinkle with salt and pepper inside and out. Melt butter in a roasting pan, add ham and duckling. Brown it quickly on both sides under the broiler. Lower oven temperature to 350F. Pour Madeira wine over duckling. Add some of the chicken stock, salt and pepper, and cover with buttered waxpaper. Roast 1 to 1-1/2 hours, occasionally adding the remaining chicken stock.

<content-ref src='/page/25/Picture/0'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/25/Text/1'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/25/Text/2'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/25/Text/3'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/25/SectionHeader/4'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/25/ListGroup/5'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/25/Text/6'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/25/Text/7'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/25/Text/8'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/25/Text/9'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/25/Text/10'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/25/Text/11'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/25/Text/12'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/25/PageFooter/13'></content-ref>
Transfer duckling to a heated platter. Skim fat from pan drippings and strain into a saucepan. Add flour and slowly cook over low heat until the mixture thickens.
Quarter duckling, serve with the sauce, boiled potatoes, vegetables.
Serves 4 – Preparation time: 1 hour 30 minutes
Rabbit with paprika sauce - Králik na paprice

• • 1 rabbit, 4.5 lbs., skinned, cleaned, cut in pieces
  • • 3 slices bacon, cut in strips
  • • 1/3 cup vegetable oil
  • • 1 small onion, finely chopped
  • • 3 tablespoons paprika
  • • 6 grains each of whole allspice and black peppercorns
  • • thyme, 2 bay leaves
  • • 3 tablespoons flour
  • • 2 cups chicken stock
  • • 1.1/2 cups sour cream
  • • salt
Rinse, pat dry rabbit pieces. Sprinkle with salt and lard each with bacon strips.
Heat oil in a large pan; add onion and cook until translucent. Add paprika, whole allspice, black peppercorns, thyme, bay leaves and rabbit pieces.
Simmer, covered, for 1.1/2 hours, or until rabbit is tender, adding chicken stock when needed.
Using a slotted spoon, lift rabbit pieces from liquid and place in a casserole.

Stir flour into the liquid and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes. Add remaining chicken stock and sour cream and cook, stirring as necessary, until sauce is reduced to desired consistency, about 5 minutes. Strain sauce over rabbit. Simmer until heated through.
Serve with gnocchi, dumplings, noodles.
Serves 6 – Preparation time: 2 hours

<content-ref src='/page/26/PageHeader/0'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/26/SectionHeader/1'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/26/ListGroup/2'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/26/Text/3'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/26/Text/4'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/26/SectionHeader/5'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/26/ListGroup/6'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/26/Text/7'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/26/Text/8'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/26/PageFooter/9'></content-ref>
Fried rabbit - Králik smažený

• • 1 rabbit, 4-5 lbs., skinned, cleaned, cut in small serving portions
  • • 2 eggs, whole
  • • 1/4 cup milk
  • • 3/4 cup flour
  • • 1-1/2 cups bread crumbs
  • • 1 cup vegetable oil for frying
  • • salt

Scald rabbit with hot water, pat dry. Pound each piece lightly, sprinkle with salt. Dredge each in flour shaking off excess, dip in mixture of beaten eggs and milk, coat with bread crumbs. Fry in hot oil until golden, about 5 minutes each side. Drain on paper towel. Serve with salad, vegetables, potatoes.
Serves 6 – Preparation time: 45 minutes
Roast hare (or wild rabbit) - Zajic pečený

• • Hindquarters of 1 hare, 4-5 lbs., cleaned, membrane removed
  • • 3 slices bacon, cut in short strips (1")
  • • 1 medium onion, finely chopped
  • • 8 tablespoons butter
  • • 1-2 cups beef stock
  • • salt and pepper

Rinse, pat dry hare. Lard meaty side with bacon strips, sprinkle with salt and pepper. Melt butter in a roasting pan, add onion and the hare. Roast at 350F for 45 minutes, larded side down. Turn hare larded side up and roast 30-40 minutes or until tender. Baste frequently with beef stock and juices from the pan. Cut hare in serving portions. Serve with pan juices, fried potatoes, noodles, vegetables.
Serves 6 – Preparation time: 1-2 hours

<content-ref src='/page/27/PageHeader/0'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/27/SectionHeader/1'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/27/ListGroup/2'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/27/Text/3'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/27/Text/4'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/27/Text/5'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/27/Text/6'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/27/Text/7'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/27/Text/8'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/27/Text/9'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/27/Text/10'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/27/Text/11'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/27/Text/12'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/27/Text/13'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/27/PageFooter/14'></content-ref>
Hare in cream sauce - Zajic na smetanë

• • Hindquarters of 1 hare, 4-5 lbs., cleaned, membrane removed
  • • 3 slices bacon cut in short strips
  • • 1 medium onion, finely chopped
  • • carrot, celery, parsnip – sliced
  • • 5 grains each of black peppercorn, whole allspice, juniper berries
  • • thyme, bay leaf, ground nutmeg
  • • 6 tablespoons butter
  • • 1-1/2 cups beef stock
  • • 1-1/2 cups heavy cream
  • • juice of 1-2 lemons
  • • 3 tablespoons flour
  • • salt and pepper
Rinse the hare, pat dry. Rub with crushed juniper berries, sprinkle with salt, lard with bacon strips.
Melt butter in a heavy skillet, add onion and vegetables, and sauté over medium heat.
When onion is translucent, add hare and brown evenly on all sides.
Transfer all into a roaster. Add spices and some of the beef stock.
Roast 1 hour at 350F larded side down, then turn hare larded side up and continue roasting until tender, about 1 hour. Baste frequently with pan juices and beef stock.
Remove hare to carving board.

Make sauce by combining pan juices with flour. Simmer 5 minutes, stirring constantly. Add juice of 1 lemon and cream. Simmer a little more. Season to taste with salt, pepper and more lemon juice, if needed. Strain.
To serve, slice hare and place slices on a warmed platter. Pour sauce over top.
Serve remaining sauce in a gravy boat.
Serve with rice, noodles, vegetables.
Serves 6 – Preparation time: 2 hours 30 minutes

<content-ref src='/page/28/PageHeader/0'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/28/SectionHeader/1'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/28/SectionHeader/2'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/28/ListGroup/3'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/28/SectionHeader/4'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/28/ListGroup/5'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/28/SectionHeader/6'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/28/Text/7'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/28/Text/8'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/28/Text/9'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/28/Text/10'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/28/Text/11'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/28/Text/12'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/28/Text/13'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/28/Text/14'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/28/Text/15'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/28/Text/16'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/28/Text/17'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/28/Text/18'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/28/Text/19'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/28/Text/20'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/28/PageFooter/21'></content-ref>
Marinated hare in wine sauce - Zajic na černo
Marinade:

• • 1 cup sliced carrots
  • • 1 cup sliced onions
  • • 1 cup sliced shallots
  • • 3 cloves garlic, crushed
  • • 10 black peppercorns
  • • 3 bay leaves
  • • thyme
  • • 1/4 cup cognac
  • • 3 cups red wine
  • • 1-1/2 cups vegetable oil
Hare and sauce:

• • Front part of 1 hare, 4-5 lbs.
  • • 4 tablespoons butter
  • • 3 oz. bacon, diced
  • • 1 medium onion, chopped
  • • 3 tablespoons vinegar
  • • 1-1/2 cups beef stock
  • • 1 cup red wine
  • • grated rind of 1 lemon
  • • 5 grains each of black peppercorns and whole allspice
  • • 2 bay leaves, thyme
  • • 4 tablespoons flour
  • • 2 tablespoons brown sugar
  • • 1/4 cup cranberry sauce
  • • salt and pepper
To marinate:
Place hare in a large crock. Add all dry ingredients, top with cognac, add wine.
Add oil to seal air out. The hare must be submerged in the marinade. Soak hare overnight, or even better 2-3 days.
Remove and wipe dry with a cloth.

Heat butter in a 4 quart top-of-range casserole. Add bacon and onion and cook until soft. Add all spices and lemon rind. Sprinkle hare with salt and vinegar, put into casserole, and brown lightly on all sides.
Reduce heat. Add some of the beef stock.
Cover tightly and simmer 1-1-1/2 hours, or until meat is tender when pierced with a fork. Add beef stock occasionally.
Transfer hare to a heated platter.
Skim off fat from the cooking liquid, stir in the flour and continue cooking to a rich brown. Add the remaining beef stock and the wine.
Cook until sauce thickens. Strain, blend in sugar and cranberry sauce. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Bring to boil, stirring constantly.
Slice hare, pour hot sauce over top.
Serve with noodles, gnocchi, dumplings.
Serves 6 – Preparation time: 2 hours, plus marinating
⇒ Venison in cream sauce – same as Hare in cream sauce
Venison in wine sauce – same as Marinated hare in wine sauce

<content-ref src='/page/29/PageHeader/0'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/29/SectionHeader/1'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/29/ListGroup/2'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/29/Text/3'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/29/Text/4'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/29/Text/5'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/29/Text/6'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/29/Text/7'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/29/SectionHeader/8'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/29/ListGroup/9'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/29/Text/10'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/29/PageFooter/11'></content-ref>
Venison cutlets, or medallions - Srnči žebírka

• • 12 young venison cutlets, or medallions, 3 oz. ea.
  • • 12 juniper berries, crushed
  • • 4 tablespoons cognac
  • • salt and pepper
  • • 1·1/2 cups sour cream
  • • 1/2 cup chicken broth
  • • 3/4 cup olive oil
  • • 4 tablespoons butter
  • • 1 small onion, finely chopped
  • • 1 lb. fresh mushrooms, sliced lengthwise
  • • snipped parsley
Trim excess fat from the cutlets, pound them lightly, rub with juniper berries, sprinkle with salt and pepper, drizzle with cognac and olive oil. Cover, marinate at least 1 hour.
Meanwhile melt butter in a large skillet, sauté onion and mushrooms. Season with salt and pepper. Reserve.

Drain and wipe the cutlets, reserve marinade. Heat remaining oil in a heavy frying pan, fry venison over high heat, about 3 minutes each side. Remove cutlets, keep them warm. Deglaze pan with marinade. Add chicken broth and sour cream, simmer 5 minutes. Taste for salt and pepper.
Coat the cutlets, or medallions, with the sauce. Garnish with mushrooms, snipped parsley, poached halves of apples, serve with noodles, rice.
Serves 6 – Preparation time: 20 minutes, plus marinating
Roast pheasant - Bažant pečený

• • 1 pheasant
  • • 2 slices bacon cut in short strips
  • • 6 tablespoons butter
  • • 1 medium onion, finely chopped
  • • 3·4 tablespoons flour
  • • 1·1/2 cups chicken broth
  • • salt and pepper

Rinse and wipe the pheasant inside and out. Lard the breast and thighs with bacon strips. Brown the pheasant evenly all around in a frying pan in half of the butter and onion. Preheat oven to 350F. Transfer pheasant, breast down, into an ovenproof deep dish together with the butter and onion from the frying pan. Add salt and pepper. Roast 30·40 minutes, until the top gets reddish. Baste often with the remaining butter and chicken broth. Turn the bird breast side up, continue roasting in the same manner, 40-45 minutes.

<content-ref src='/page/30/PageHeader/0'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/30/Text/1'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/30/Text/2'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/30/SectionHeader/3'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/30/ListGroup/4'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/30/Text/5'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/30/Text/6'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/30/Text/7'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/30/SectionHeader/8'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/30/ListGroup/9'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/30/Text/10'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/30/PageFooter/11'></content-ref>

On the stove top bring the pan juices to boil. Add flour and cook 5 minutes stirring constantly. Add the remaining chicken broth and cook a little more. When the sauce thickens, strain it and pour over pheasant, cut in four portion sizes. Serve with red cabbage, potatoes, cranberries.
Serves 4 – Preparation time: 1 hour 30 minutes
Pheasant in cream sauce - Bažant na smetanë

• • 1 pheasant
  • • 6 tablespoons butter
  • • 2 slices bacon cut in short strips
  • • 1 medium onion, finely chopped
  • • 1 cup chicken broth
  • • 1-1/2 cups heavy cream
  • • 2 tablespoons grated horseradish
  • • 1 tablespoon cognac
  • • juice of 1 lemon
  • • salt and pepper

Rinse and wipe the pheasant inside and out. Lard the breast and thighs with bacon strips. Roast pheasant as indicated in "Roast pheasant". In a saucepan blend pan juices, cream and horseradish. Cook for 5 minutes over medium heat. Add cognac and lemon juice. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Strain.
Pour some gravy over the pheasant cut in 4 portions. Serve remaining gravy separately. Serve with rice, vegetables.
Serves 4 – Preparation time: 1 hour 30 minutes
Partridge/Quail - Koroptev/Křepelka

• • 6 quails
  • • 3 slices bacon
  • • 6 tablespoons butter
  • • 1 cup chicken broth, or water
  • • salt and pepper

Rinse quails, pat dry. Sprinkle with salt and pepper inside and outside. Place 1/2 slice bacon inside each. Heat butter in a flameproof casserole, add quails. Roast 40-50 minutes at 350F. Baste often with pan drippings, chicken broth or water. Serve dish straight from the oven with quails cut in halves.

<content-ref src='/page/31/PageHeader/0'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/31/Text/1'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/31/Text/2'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/31/SectionHeader/3'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/31/Text/4'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/31/Text/5'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/31/SectionHeader/6'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/31/Text/7'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/31/Text/8'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/31/ListGroup/9'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/31/ListGroup/10'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/31/PageFooter/11'></content-ref>

Garnish with fresh parsley sprigs, red cabbage, cranberry sauce, poached halves of apples.
Serve with rice, lentils.
Serves 6 – Preparation time: 1 hour
Baked carp - Kapr pečený

Arrange carp steaks in a single layer in a well oiled baking pan.
Season with caraway seeds, salt and pepper. Bake at 350F 25-30
minutes, or until fish flakes easily when tested with a fork.
In a saucepan heat butter until lightly browned. Pour over fish.
Garnish with lemon wedges.
Serve with potatoes, vegetables, salad.
Serves 6 – Preparation time: 40 minutes
Fried carp - Kapr smažený

Soak fish 30 minutes in lightly salted milk. Dredge each piece in flour,
dip in beaten eggs, coat with bread crumbs. Fry in hot oil until golden,
about 4 minutes each side. Drain on paper towel.
Serve on lettuce lined platter, garnish with lemon wedges and parsley
sprigs.
Serve with potato salad, green salad, vegetables.
Serves 6 – Preparation time: 1 hour

• • 6 carp steaks, 3-4 lbs.
  • • 1/2 cup vegetable oil
  • • 6 tablespoons butter
  • • 2 teaspoons caraway seeds
  • • salt and pepper

• • 6 carp steaks, 3-4 lbs.
  • • 2 cups milk
  • • 3/4 cup flour
  • • 2 eggs
  • • 1 cup bread crumbs
  • • 1 cup vegetable oil for frying
  • • salt

<content-ref src='/page/32/PageHeader/0'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/32/SectionHeader/1'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/32/ListGroup/2'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/32/Text/3'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/32/Text/4'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/32/Text/5'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/32/Text/6'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/32/Text/7'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/32/Text/8'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/32/SectionHeader/9'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/32/ListGroup/10'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/32/Text/11'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/32/Text/12'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/32/Text/13'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/32/Text/14'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/32/Text/15'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/32/PageFooter/16'></content-ref>
Carp with paprika sauce - Kapr na paprice

• • 6 carp steaks, 3-4 lbs.
  • • 1-1/2 cups water or fish broth
  • • 6 tablespoons butter
  • • 1 medium onion, finely chopped
  • • parsley, finely chopped
  • • 2 tablespoons paprika
  • • salt
  • • 3 tablespoons butter and 4 tablespoons flour for the roux

Optional: 1/2 cup heavy cream
Melt butter in a large saucepot, add onion and cook until translucent. Add parsley and paprika, simmer 3 minutes. Add the fish and some of the fish broth or water.
Cover and simmer 15-20 minutes.
Using a slotted spatula, lift the carp portions onto a heated platter. For sauce, melt butter in a skillet and stir in flour. Cook and stir until golden.

Add cooking liquid from the carp and some of the fish broth if needed. Cook until sauce thickens. Optional: for a creamier sauce blend in heavy cream. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Strain over fish. Serve with mashed potatoes, rice, tomato salad.
Serves 6 – Preparation time: 45 minutes
⇔ Perch, Pike, or Trout with paprika sauce – Candát, Štika, Pstruh na paprice. – same as Carp with paprika sauce –
Baked pike with sour cream - Štika pečená se smetanou

• • 1 pike, 4 lbs., cleaned, with head and tail left on
  • • 2 bacon slices cut in thin strips
  • • 6 tablespoons butter
  • • 1 medium onion, finely chopped
  • • 4 medium potatoes, parboiled, sliced
  • • juice of 1 lemon
  • • 2 teaspoons paprika
  • • salt
  • • 1 pint sour cream
Sauté onion in butter.

Meanwhile, sprinkle pike with salt, paprika and lemon juice. Lard with strips of bacon. Lay fish in a lightly greased baking pan. Arrange potato slices on sides of fish and up, towards the edge of the pan. Sprinkle some salt over potatoes.
Pour the butter onion mixture over fish. Top with sour cream. Bake at 350F, 30-40 minutes.
Serve with tomato salad, vegetables.
Serves 6 – Preparation time: 1 hour

<content-ref src='/page/33/PageHeader/0'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/33/SectionHeader/1'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/33/ListGroup/2'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/33/SectionHeader/3'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/33/ListGroup/4'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/33/Text/5'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/33/Text/6'></content-ref><content-ref src='/page/33/PageFooter/7'></content-ref>
Salmon trout with dill sauce - Pstruh s koprovou omáčkou

• • 6 trouts, 4 lbs., cleaned, with heads and tails left on
  • • 1/2 bottle white wine
  • • 1.1/2 quarts water
  • • 1 medium onion, quartered
  • • juice of one lemon
  • • 10 black peppercorns
  • • 2 bay leaves
  • • 6 tablespoons butter
  • • parsley, finely chopped
  • • salt
Sauce:

• • 3 tablespoons butter and 4 tablespoons flour
  • • 2 tablespoons finely chopped dill
  • • 1 small onion, finely chopped
  • • parsley, finely chopped
  • • 2 cups fish broth
  • • 1 tablespoon vinegar
  • • 1 teaspoon sugar
  • • 1/2 cup heavy cream
  • • salt

Heat the wine, water, onion, lemon juice, bay leaves and peppercorns. Simmer 10 minutes. Add the trouts and simmer gently for 15 minutes, without boiling.

Drain fish, arrange on a heated serving platter, keep it warm. Strain the broth from the fish, reserve 2 cups for dill sauce. Meanwhile, prepare the sauce. Melt butter in a saucepan, blend in flour, stir and cook until golden. Add onion, parsley, fish broth, vinegar, sugar, salt. Cook, uncovered, until sauce thickens. Strain. Blend in the cream and chopped dill. Heat through, do not boil. Pour hot butter over trouts, garnish with parsley. Hand sauce separately.
Serves 6 – Preparation time: 45 minutes
